@graph.name: Commercial Terms & Cost Drivers
@graph.description: Commercial terms and cost drivers for senior moving. The company's terms are few and exact: one flat price agreed in writing before move day; no hourly clock, ever; and no senior price, discount, deposit, or fee published — the page FAQ states directly that no special senior price or discount is offered. Everything beyond this paragraph is labeled domain education from published industry sources, never this company's prices. The market prices senior moves both ways: straight hourly for shorter local jobs, flat rate for larger, long-distance, or fixed-budget moves, with hybrid models in between. Senior move-management support — a separate profession from the mover — is published at $40–$80 per hour in mover guides and about $60–$120 per hour in AARP-cited guidance, with complete projects commonly $1,000–$3,000 or more depending on size and complexity. Published move-cost ranges: local moves about $600–$3,500; long-distance moves of roughly 1,000 miles about $1,500–$8,300, depending on shipment size and service level. Deposit practice varies by mover — published market examples run from no deposit to 10–50% — and is a market observation, not a rule. Domain cost drivers: home size; amount and type of belongings; distance; packing and unpacking scope; sorting and downsizing time; building access; time of year; crew size. Some movers publish AARP, veteran, or senior discounts; this company does not — its published position is one flat rate for every customer. No valuation offering is published for senior moves, and in company copy valuation is never presented as insurance. Senior moves with storage needs price storage on the confirmed storage basis — per job, monthly, or by volume — with no storage rate published.

@graph.name: Buyer Personas & Trigger Events
@graph.description: Buyer personas and trigger events for senior moving. The downsizing senior: decades in one home, moving to something smaller; weighs trust, keepsake care, pace, and one price in writing. The community mover: a senior with a community move-in date at an assisted-living, independent-living, or 55+ community; weighs timing certainty and price certainty. The closer-to-family mover: relocating nearer to children or family; weighs remote coordination and a human-made estimate. The adult-child coordinator: often out of town, arranging a parent's move; weighs one accountable provider, costs in writing, and communication — the published audience the survey room's remote walkthrough is built for. The estate handler (a domain persona; this company's estate scope is not published): a family member or estate handler after a death or settlement, weighing discretion, keepsake care, and exact placement. Trigger events: a move-in date set; the downsizing decision; a home sale or closing; a family proximity decision; an estate settlement; a health change (a motivation only, never a care claim). Domain buying logic, labeled as such: the decision pace is slower than a standard residential move, because decisions tied to decades of personal history take time, and an unhurried pace is itself a buying criterion. Search behavior: families search generically — 'senior moving' and 'senior movers near me', both ranking first for this site in Search Console data — and adult children often search from out of town on a parent's behalf. Senior-household clients rarely post public reviews, for privacy; per the owner, low review volume is expected and is not a quality signal, and the per-branch Google ratings (Winchester 5.0 from 1 review, Martinsburg 4.7 from 6) are branch ratings, never presented as senior-specific ratings.
